findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with black biological growth. The person in charge (PIC) was informed. The PIC stated that the general manager is responsible for cleaning the machine. Ensure that the ice machine remains clean to sight and touch at all times to prevent contamination of ice. A follow-up will be conducted on September 21, 2026 to ensure the interior and exterior of the ice machine has been cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed walk-in freezer to have rusty ice accumulating from the ceiling. There are tubs at the top of the shelf capturing the ice. The PIC stated that the trays must be emptied weekly to accommodate the flow of water. Ensure repairs are conducted to prevent rust contamination with food items stored in the freezer.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer bucket and triple sink in kitchen to measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia. PIC claimed that dispenser has been malfunctioning for some time. A different staff member was able to disassemble and replace to the nozzle of the dispenser. The sanitizer solution from the dispenser measured 100ppm quaternary ammonia after repair. The triple sink and sanitizer bucket was refilled with proper solution. This violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed three knives in the prep area metal rack to be soiled with food debris. The knives were removed from the rack and were placed in the ware-washing area to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure staff are cleaning all equipment and utensils frequently enough to avoid accumulation of food debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed walk-in freezer to have rusty ice accumulating from the ceiling. There are tubs at the top of the shelf capturing the ice. The tubs were fairly full, suggesting the leak has been present for some time. Ensure repairs are conducted to prevent rust contamination with food items stored in the freezer.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed two jackets stored on dry storage shelves containing food. PIC was informed that employees need to use a designated area for personal item storage to prevent cross contamination. There seems to be a designated clothing rack in the office for personal items. Ensure staff are using this space rather than dry storage shelving for personal items.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed floors underneath dry storage shelves in back of facility to be soiled with food debris and refuse. Clean floors underneath shelving. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed door handle of walk in cooler to be broken. Fix walk in cooler door handle. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed food employee put on a new pair of gloves without first washing hands. Wash hands each time before putting on new gloves. Discussed proper glove use with PIC.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed interior of kitchen ice machine to be soiled with mold and debris. Clean and sanitize interior of kitchen ice machine.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed quaternary ammonia solution in sanitizer bucket to test at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. Solution was remade and tested at 200 ppm. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed no quaternary ammonia test strips available for use in facility. Provide test strips for all sanitizers in use at facility. 

4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed wet mop head stored head down in mop bucket. Store wet mop head in inverted fashion to promote drying.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
The person in charge states that she has a certified manager license but does not know how to obtain the number. The person in charge shall be a Certified Food Protection Manager. Provide enough certified employees for the facility to be under the charge of a Certified Food Protection Manager at all times. 
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed tomato on the prep line to have an internal temperature of 50F.  The lettuce and spinach are 44F and 42F respectively. The tomato is stored between these two items. The tomato was discarded approximately one inch of sliced tomato in the bottom. Fresh tomato was placed in the space from the back stock cooler which is holding food at around 30F. 
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment: 3-201.11: Observed chili being heated up that was from the day before. The chili was cooled after closing on 11-19 and was being reheated for service on 11-20. Cooling and reheating is a Class 1 activity, and class 2 facilities are not permitted to cool and reheat foods. Ensure cooling and reheating practices no longer occur in order to stay within permit requirements. The chili was discarded during the inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Observed soda nozzles to be soiled. Also, the area behind the soda nozzles was soiled with mildew and other debris. The manager stated soda nozzles are cleaned at least once per week. Ensure soda nozzles are cleaned more frequently so they are maintained clean to sight and touch. Soda nozzles were cleaned during the inspection. 
(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: The facility had quat test strips available for use; however, there were no chlorine test strips available. Because both kinds of sanitizers are used, both kinds of test strips must be available for use. Ensure chlorine test strips are provided. Test strips were given to the facility to correct the violation. 
A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: Observed the mop to be stored in the mop sink from the night before in a position that did not allow it to air dry properly. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to air dry. 
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14  (P) Employee changed gloves without washing hands between tasks. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14. Employee answered phone and then put gloves on without washing hands. Employee was coached on hand washing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizer at 0ppm at knife holder on line. Quat sanitizer is 0 ppm at 3 compartment sink sanitizer bay. Provide proper chemical concentrations for sanitizers as listed on labels. Reference 4-501.114. Proper sanitizer was added to the knife container. Candi was at the facility and had parts to fix the sanitizer dispenser.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: 4-204-112  (C) A thermometer is not provided in the walk in cooler. Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112. Provide thermometer as required.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: 4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14. Test kit was provided at time of inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-603.16  (C) Observed an employee washing and sanitizing the customer dishes but not rinsing the dishes. The rinsing step is important to remove any remaining detergent and food debris, to avoid diluting or inactivating the sanitizer. Employee was shown the proper way to rinse off the dishes before sanitizing. Reference 4-603.16. Employee was coached on proper use of the 3 part sink.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on racks over 3 part sink. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) [Floors, Walls along base board are and door jambs are found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily clean able. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antis lip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily clean able.  Reference 6-201.11.  Repair areas along base cove and door jambs which need repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-501.110  (C) Employees were found not using the designated dressing rooms / changing areas or designated employees lockers when changing clothes or storing personal articles. Dressing rooms and lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used if employees regularly change clothes or store personal articles in the establishment while working. Reference 6-501.110. Observed a coat to be placed on prep table during the inspection. Store personal belongings properly and form good habits for storage. Coat was moved to coat rack area provided.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Top layers of sliced tomatoes, roast beef, and cold cut combo were observed with surface temperatures of 46F-57F; 46F-60F; and 47F-52F respectively. Product above 41F was observed to be stacked above the fill line in containers at the cold baine. Surface temperatures for product deeper in containers was observed at 44F/below. Roast beef and sliced tomatoes had internal temperatures of 36F and 40f respectively for product well below the fill line of the container. Top layers of roast beef, sliced tomatoes, and cold cut combo were removed from containers to be inventoried and discarded.

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, display and service.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Chunky mold buildup was observed on the ceiling inside the ice machine around the opening where ice dispenses. Store manager removed the cover to the top tray/filter area, and very thick mold accumulation was present throughout the machine. A sticker inside the machine showed the last date of cleaning to be in August of 2015. Manager turned off the machine to begin cleaning and sanitizing.
NOTE: The ice machine needs to be on a routine schedule for cleaning and sanitizing to eliminate buildup of mold.

Food shall be protected from cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Staff were observed working the register and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to return make line for food prep. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. Employees began washing hands between tasks as needed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time they may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves, between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
(Educational handouts on glove use and proper handwashing provided)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - The following were observed to be in disrepair:
A) walkin cooler shelves (chipping paint/rusty);  and
B) wire storage rack above dirty dish drain board (chipping pain/rusty).
Clean and re-seal the abovementioned items.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Facility uses bleach solution for wiping down white bowls and minimizing discoloration. Chlorine test kit was not present for checking bleach solution concentration. Obtain and use chlorine test kit for checking bleach solution.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
720.820 - A) Sanitizer solution at 3 part sink with dishes in it was observed at 100ppm quat. Solution was murky and appeared to have been in use for some time. Quat solution was then dispensed directly in a separate container to check the concentration but was not registering above 100ppm. Manager let the chemical run through the line for several seconds prior to checking the concentration again. The sanitizer was not registering at proper concentration. Solution at 3 part sink was remade by manually mixing sanitizer to get proper concentration (200ppm). A call for service needs to be made for the dispenser. Until the wall mounted chemical dispenser is working properly all staff must be educated on manually mixing sanitizer and use of test strips to ensure proper concentration is maintained.

B) Employee rinsed a knife used for cutting bread at the front handsink, and then placed the knife back on the make line. Other knives were taken to the 3 part sink to go through ware washing and brought back in less time than it would take to properly sanitize utensils. All knives were taken to the dish area and placed through ware washing again. Employee was advised items must be submerged in sanitizer for at least 1 minute prior to removing to air dry.
Educate staff on proper manual ware washing process. (educational handout provided)

 Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
(R) 750.800b - Back of soda machine ice shoot was soiled with mold buildup. Clean and sanitize the ice shoot as needed to eliminate buildup of mold.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate the buildup of mold and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
(R) 750.800e - Surface of sprayer was soiled with grimy black buildup. Clean the sprayer surface daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.

Clean all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Restroom door self closers were broken. Repair or replace the self closers on the restroom doors.

All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
(R) 750.1200 & 1220 - A) hole was observed in the floor along the wall below the paper towel dispenser in the women's room. Re-seal the floor where disrepair is present in the women's room.

B) Coving was loose/missing along the floor to wall juncture at the south wall next to the register. Debris accumulation was observed in the area. Clean the aforementioned area and re-seal the floor to wall juncture.

C) The floor between the counter and wall at the drink counter was soiled with black, grimy buildup. Clean the floor in this area.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean. Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
(R) 750.1220 - Men's' room handsink was not sealed to the wall. Caulk the juncture between the wall and the sink in the men's room.

Walls and attached equipment must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1320 - Spray bottle labeled bleach had a yellowish color to it. Manager stated it was a diluted solution of bleach and water used for wiping out white bowls to help minimize discoloration. Solution bleached out the inspector's test strip and was basically straight bleach. Solution was diluted to be at 200ppm chlorine.
Maintain bleach solution at 100-200ppm, and use test strips to verify concentration.

Chemicals must not be used in a manner that may pose a risk of cross contamination or a potential hazard to persons exposed to the chemicals.
